items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: I didn't know him personally at all. I didn't know Joe Oliver.

ctx.x: Him. Mm-hmm. How would Joe Oliver do it?

Well, Joe Oliver did too. It's like I'm telling you, I didn't know much about him. The only time I saw Joe, when I first went to Chicago, I went to a place to call the plantation. Uh-huh. And I went to the Yuddy Band and I went there and heard him. But I didn't know him personally at all. I didn't know Joe Oliver.
What about out in the country? Did they play trumpet pretty much the same as in the city? Did they use the same tricks?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-08-20
items.q: I didn't ever see Joe Oliver until I went to Chicago.

ctx.x: You wouldn't know my band might go there.

No. I didn't never get to see him. I don't mean I wasn't old enough to see him, but I just never, I'll tell you the man I first seen when I was kind of getting on my feet with Trumpet, the first man I seen, I ain't gonna lie, it was Bunk Johnson. I seen him on my excursion pass our home recently, going to Homer, Louisiana, and I went on that excursion and I saw him play. First time. And I didn't ever see Joe Oliver until I went to Chicago.
That's a funny thing, you can live in the same town with people and never hear him.

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: I didn't know King Oliver until I went to Chicago and so on. I didn't know them.

ctx.x: Sure. Sure, I know him. Where was he from? Do you remember anybody? Tell him he's from Milwaukee. I don't know. I don't know. Guys, that guy didn't tell you where the real home was. But we had a fella named Ed Ellis used to play trombone. Talked properly, you know. Every time somebody asked him, he was a little bit of a guitar.

I was wondering about somebody at that. Did you know Jimmy Blank, the piano player? Sure. I know him. I know him. I know him. I know him. I know him. I know him. I know him. I know him. I know him. I know him. I know him. But stuff says New York. So I asked him again, he says, tell him my home is in Philly. So he got sick, see. And he got really sick. Didn't nobody know what to do for everybody. So where was his people and everything. So he called his wife. His wife was named Stella. He said, what is it? He said,…
I believe he left there in 22 didn't he? Joe, I think before then, 1918. Yeah, I didn't know him. He was in the Army when he left here again. Sure, I didn't know him.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: And the first time I seen him was when I went to Chicago. I didn't never see him down here. First time I saw him. I went to Chicago to the plantation one night... And that's the first time I seen King Oliver.

ctx.x: Was Joe Oliver doing anything like him at all?
